To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1), in hypertensives, obesity is associated with a more pronounced elevation of blood pressure during maximal exercise, indicating a higher risk for the development of coronary heart disease in these subjects; (2) during moderate exercise (stage 2 of the treadmill protocol), hypertensives have significantly higher blood pressures than normotensive, and (3) during maximal exercise, the obese hypertensives have higher blood pressures and heart rate than the lean hypertensives.

the blood pressure response to exercise in obese and lean adolescents with essential hypertension.
the identification of hypertensive adolescents and their early treatment.
the identification of mechanisms that may be involved in the pathophysiology of hypertension in adolescents.
